title: Resource efficient federated edge learning with hyperdimensional computing

pse.problem: Resource constraints in federated Hyper-Dimensional Computing (HDC) training result in sacrificed predictive performance.
pse.solution_function: The Resource-Efficient Federated Hyper-Dimensional Computing (RE-FHDC) framework trains and fine-tunes multiple smaller independent HDC sub-models, achieving comparable or higher predictive performance and lower processing times.
pse.solution_structure: The full-sized HDC model is divided into multiple HDC sub-models. Each sub-model is trained on different devices (nodes or edge devices). The server aggregates the HDC sub-models and concatenates them to create the full-sized HDC model.
pse.solution_implementation: Upon reception of the full-sized HDC model, devices select one or more identical subsets of positions from the full-sized HDC model and apply iterative training to these subsets. A position refers to a particular index of each hyperdimensional prototype or as a column of a CD matrix representing the HDC model.
pse.effect: Reduced computational and communication costs, lower processing times, comparable or higher predictive performance compared to conventional federated HDC implementation.
